name: Queenie R. Ridulme
half:
Queenie R. Ridulme has advised 19 theses in this repository between 2020 and 2026. Their research supervision focuses heavily on nursing and patient care, which accounts for 18 items. Other supervised sub-topics include management and leadership (6), mental health and well-being (4), public health and COVID-19 (4), environment and sustainability (3), climate and disaster (2), culture and identity (2), higher education (1), governance and public policy (1), and arts and creative practice (1). They have an advisee in the latest year, 2026.

Their own research includes two articles in this repository. One article, published in 2023, examines the menopausal experiences of Dumagat women, covering gender and inclusion and mental health and well-being. Another article from 2018 focuses on public health and COVID-19 through the development of a counselling framework for mothers of children with perinatally acquired HIV disease.

Supervision patterns show a strong interest in international nursing contexts, including studies in Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, Bahrain, the USA, and the Philippines. Research topics under their guidance include work-life balance, resilience, job satisfaction, leadership styles, psychological safety, burnout, and organizational commitment. They have supervised studies involving various settings, such as tertiary hospitals, government hospitals, and academic hospitals. Evidence of their research focus is primarily centered on nursing professional efficacy and psychological well-being.
